Column: Readers have a lot to say about our critique of Northwestern’s new Ryan Field

A national ground stoppage is a good time to reply to emails about the issues surrounding the new Ryan Field at Northwestern.

Ground Stoppage Saturday was a fine day for college football’s elite teams to try to make their statements for the CFP rankings.

In airport bars and restaurants all across America, TVs were tuned in to college games as weary travelers still stranded from Friday’s FAA ground stoppage awaited word on their next flight delay while munching on chicken wings and cursing their airlines, airports and airheaded Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.

It was a day of chaos for tens of thousands of passengers, but please don’t forget those anxious fans dealing with new kickoff times the delays and canceled flights caused.

“Some games are being moved,” Duffy said Saturday morning. “That’s not the most important thing, but we do want to move teams around the country, so we can have playoffs happen.”

Of course. Saving the playoffs was obviously the first thing we all thought of when watching the massive disruption allegedly caused by a routing issue.

Any Comcast customer knows the fix is simple: Unplug the router, wait 10 seconds, plug it back in and hit reset. If that doesn’t work, schedule a service appointment for next Tuesday in a window from 2-6 p.m.

But since no one thought of that, Americans had a communal experience combining two of our holiday staples, football and travel nightmares.

As someone who recently spent more time taxiing on the tarmac than the actual flight from Cleveland to Chicago, I feel the pain of disgruntled passengers stuck at O’Hare. (If you’re reading this while stranded in Terminal B, there’s a Garrett Popcorn kiosk nearby, and Skip Bayless’ brother has a decent restaurant there. Just don’t mention Skip to Rick).

Sitting in an airport while fuming about the transportation industry is usually a good time to answer the work emails you ignored during the week. And since my inbox was flooded with comments about new Ryan Field after I inadvertently upset stadium developer Pat Ryan Jr. for mentioning the obstructed press box view, I’ll just pretend I’m at the Billy Goat in Terminal C.

Here are a few thoughtful comments from readers.

Comment: “Maybe if you paid to sit on the 50-yard line, you would have more of a right to criticize the new stadium. … Pay and maybe you’ll get a better seat.”
